videos.script: Last lesson compared four engines. This one is about a fifth, and it gets a lesson to itself for a reason that is not technical. {{fifth}} Oracle Database is where a great deal of the world's money lives. Banks, insurers, telephone companies, tax authorities, hospital systems. If you work in a large organisation you will meet it, and you will probably not be the person who installed it. {{where}} It is a capable relational database and everything in this course applies to it. What makes it different is that it is expensive in a specific way, and that way changes how systems get built around it. {{money}} You are licensed per processor core, with a factor per chip. The features you expect to be part of a database are priced separately. The tool for finding a slow query is one of them. {{licence}} So decisions that look technical are not. A team keeps logic inside the database because that is what the licence already pays for. Nobody adds a reporting replica, because a replica is another licence. {{shape}} Then the dialect, which has real surprises. An empty string is null. There is a table called DUAL that exists to have one row in it. And a plan you read with a package call rather than a keyword. {{dialect}} One thing before we start. Every other lesson in this course ran its examples on a real server and showed you what came back. This one cannot: there is no Oracle here to run. So this lesson describes what Oracle prints, and says so every time. Nothing in it is a screen I made up. {{honest}}
